family.description: the graph's family (with graphs: the first graph's)

b.description: trig only: the period factor the stem's equation prints (cos 2x + 1: 2; tan x: 1)

x.description: [min, max, step] of the grid's x-axis (degrees for a trig graph); the learner's taps snap to the step

domain.description: [x0, x1] where the curve is drawn, when the paper limits it

kind.description: a point, or an asymptote: a horizontal / vertical line

label.description: The memo's NAME for it, never its position ('y-intercept', 'turning point', 'asymptote', 'one other point', 'x-intercept of g'); features with the same graph, kind and label are matched as a set, in any order

at.description: Where the memo puts it: [x, y] for a point, the value for a line (y = −9: -9)

alt.description: Other places the memo accepts ('ANY other point', '(45° ; −3) or (135° ; 3)'), on the grid

tol.description: How far from at (or an alt) still earns it, in the axis' units (0: the exact grid point)

marks.description: Its marks (0 when it only completes a criterion another feature carries)

crit.description: 0-based index of the memo criterion it belongs to: features (and a shape) sharing a crit earn only together ('Intercepts (2 ; 0) and (0 ; −8)', 1 mark: one carries the mark, the other 0)

graph.description: With graphs: the id of the graph it belongs to

turn.description: A turning point (the curve is flat there): the fit uses it

features.description: every feature the memo's criteria mark, in the memo's order

label.description: A NEUTRAL name for the shape, shown on its result chip ('Shape'): never the answer ('decreasing')

answer.description: The shape word the memo marks, as the builder names a curve: exponential 'increasing' / 'decreasing' (+ ', above' / ', below' its asymptote: 'increasing, above'), log 'increasing' / 'decreasing', line 'positive gradient' / 'negative gradient', parabola '∪' / '∩', cubic 'positive' / 'negative' (leading coefficient), hyperbola 'top right and bottom left' / 'top left and bottom right', tan 'increasing' / 'decreasing'; 'drawn' for any curve through the features (a sine or cosine's 'Shape'). A shorter answer is met by a longer word ('decreasing' by 'decreasing, above'); a list: any of them

crit.description: 0-based index of the memo criterion this shape belongs to (see the feature's crit)

pick.description: Only when the memo's features leave the shape open (one intercept + the asymptote fix no exponential): the words the learner chooses from (['increasing', 'decreasing']); the curve then follows the choice

graphs.description: Only for TWO graphs on one set of axes ('Sketch f and g'): each with its family and shape; every feature names its graph

anyOf.description: Only for 'Sketch / Draw the graph of f' the memo marks by its features (intercepts, turning points, asymptotes, a point, the shape): BUILT on a grid, the learner placing each feature, the curve drawn through them. Every criterion becomes features (or the shape) whose marks add up to the part's; a criterion no feature can earn ('smooth curve') is flagged. The criteria keep the memo's own text

x.description: [min, max, step] of the line: the paper's scale (the ANSWER BOOK's scaled line where it prints one, else a line that holds the answer with room either side). Every placement snaps to the step, so every memo value must be a multiple of it: 44 and 84 on a line ticked every 5 need step 1

tick.description: A short tick every so many units, as the paper's line has them (default: the step)

label.description: A number every so many units, as the paper's line prints them (default: the tick); the builder widens it on a narrow phone while the numbers would touch

unit.description: The line's quantity and unit, only when the paper's line names it ('Time (in minutes)')

tol.description: How far from the memo's value still earns it, in the line's units (0: exactly the memo's value)

at.description: The memo's five-number summary: min, q1 (the lower quartile), med (the median), q3 (the upper quartile), max

crit.description: Each value's memo criterion: the 0-based index into criteria. A criterion earns its marks only when ALL its values are right: the memo's '✓ min. & max. ✓ median ✓ Q1 and Q3' is min 0, max 0, med 1, q1 2, q3 2; '✓ box ✓ whiskers ending at 5 & 120' is q1 0, med 0, q3 0, min 1, max 1. List them in the memo's order: the result chips follow it, and the first value of a criterion shows its marks

anyOf.description: Only for 'Draw a box and whisker diagram' the memo marks by its values (min & max / the whiskers, the median, Q1 and Q3 / the box): BUILT on the paper's scaled line, the learner placing the five values, the box and whiskers drawn from them. Each memo criterion names the values it needs (crit); its marks come from criteria, in the memo's order. The criteria keep the memo's own text

x.description: [min, max, step] of the line: the paper's scale (the ANSWER BOOK's scaled line where it prints one, else a line that holds the answer with room either side). Every placement snaps to the step, so every memo value must be a multiple of it: 44 and 84 on a line ticked every 5 need step 1

tick.description: A short tick every so many units, as the paper's line has them (default: the step)

label.description: A number every so many units, as the paper's line prints them (default: the tick); the builder widens it on a narrow phone while the numbers would touch

unit.description: The line's quantity and unit, only when the paper's line names it ('Time (in minutes)')

tol.description: How far from the memo's value still earns it, in the line's units (0: exactly the memo's value)

shade.description: The memo's shading: 'left' or 'right' of ONE end (x < a, x ≥ a), 'between' two ends (a < x ≤ b), 'outside' two ends (x ≤ a or x > b)

closed.description: true: a filled dot, the end is in the answer (≤, ≥); false: an open dot (<, >)

ends.description: The memo's end: one for left / right, two for between / outside (any order)

crit.description: Each component's memo criterion: the 0-based index into criteria. 'end' is every end's place, 'circle' every end's open or filled dot, 'shade' the shading; end0 / end1 / circle0 / circle1 one end (0 the LEFT one) where the memo marks the ends apart. A criterion earns its marks only when ALL its components are right ('An open dot at −6 with an arrow to the right', 1 mark: end 0, circle 0, shade 0); a component no criterion names is not marked

anyOf.description: Only for 'Represent the answer (an inequality or interval) on a number line': BUILT on a number line, the learner choosing the shading, placing each end and choosing its dot (open or filled). Each memo criterion names the components it needs (crit); its marks come from criteria. Keep the part's 'after' when the inequality is an earlier part's answer
